reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the fluorine-effect treatment from Ti-45Al-8.5Nb (P1, P2, P9) to the HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy, but the core idea—using a fluorine treatment to form a protective Al2O3 scale—is taken almost verbatim from those passages, and the need for an anti-oxidation coating on HfNbTaTiZr is explicitly stated as future work in P4. The proposal does not combine findings from different papers into a new mechanism, nor does it provide a reason why the treatment should work on an Al-free alloy; it simply applies a known solution to a new material without integration or justification.
copied_elements: fluorine-based surface treatment (NH4F or similar) to improve oxidation resistance
formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 protective layer
reduction in mass gain as the measure of improved oxidation resistance
the fluorine effect mechanism promoting Al2O3 over less-protective oxides
the idea that a coating or surface modification is needed for HfNbTaTiZr for high-temperature air applications
